the binding of [ 3 H]glycine to brain synaptic membranes is inhibited by the noncompetitive antagonist [ 3 H]( + )‐MK‐801 and that the inhibition is potentiated by the agonist glycine.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the strychnosensitive and -insensitive glycine receptors in brain synaptic membranes and their relationship to the N‐methylene‐D‐asparate (NMDA) receptor.
the development of a method for the study of strychnine insensitive glycine binding sites in the central nervous system.
the development of a new and simple method to evaluate strychnine insensitive glycine binding in brain synaptic membranes.

the strychnin‐insensitive glycine binding is a high‐affinity binding site for glycine which may be functionally linked with the N‐metyl‐D‐asparate‐sensitive receptor channel.
the strychnosensitive and strychnineinsensitive binding sites of the glycine receptors are different from each other.

strychnine-insensitive [3H]-glycine binding sites, which are kynurenic‐acid sensitive, are functionally linked with N-methyl-D-aspartate‐sensitivereceptor channels.

we found a new binding site in the brain that is sensitive to strychnine.
we were able to show that the strychnosensitive binding sites for glycine and the MK‐801 binding site for NMDA receptors were linked.
